label.source: DailyMed metformin hydrochloride tablet, film coated, Zydus Pharmaceuticals USA Inc., setid c82a10fa-1e8e-46b6-890a-737de3f34ee1, SPL version 17, effective 2026-07-15
quotes: WARNING: LACTIC ACIDOSIS
Postmarketing cases of metformin-associated lactic acidosis have resulted in death, hypothermia, hypotension, and resistant bradyarrhythmias.

Risk factors for metformin-associated lactic acidosis include renal impairment, concomitant use of certain drugs (e.g. carbonic anhydrase inhibitors such as topiramate), age 65 years old or greater, having a radiological study with contrast, surgery and other procedures, hypoxic states (e.g., acute congestive heart failure), excessive alcohol intake, hepatic impairment
Metformin hydrochloride tablets are indicated as an adjunct to diet and exercise to improve glycemic control in adults and pediatric patients 10 years of age and older with type 2 diabetes mellitus.
Metformin may lower vitamin B12 levels.
Increased risk of hypoglycemia when used in combination with insulin and/or an insulin secretagogue.
the most common adverse reactions (>5.0%) are diarrhea, nausea/vomiting, flatulence, asthenia, indigestion, abdominal discomfort, and headache.

analysis.note: Jabbit analysis. Metformin is a cheap, decades-old prescription diabetes drug. In mice, one NIA lab study reported longer life in males, but the multi-site NIA Interventions Testing Program found metformin alone did not significantly extend lifespan (a 2024 reanalysis with a different test found a male-only effect). In people, the famous survival signal comes from observational data: a 2014 UK study found people with diabetes on metformin outlived matched people without diabetes, but a 2022 Danish register study including twins did not find that. No human trial has measured lifespan; TAME, proposed in 2016, has no ClinicalTrials.gov record. Randomized trials in older adults (MASTERS, MET-PREVENT, DEMFOS, METFORAGING) mostly missed their main goals, and MASTERS found less muscle gain from strength training. Metformin carries a boxed warning for lactic acidosis and can lower vitamin B12.
